burnaby.s1-eligibility: Rezoning applications only. Thresholds: 50+ residential units OR 1,000+ sqm commercial gross floor area. Must be in town centre or urban village zones.
burnaby.s1-budget-calculation: 1% of gross construction costs. Hard construction market costs only — excludes land acquisition, offsite servicing, permit fees, and consultant costs.
burnaby.s2-land-acknowledgement: hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓ and Sḵwx̱wú7mesh speaking peoples. Use 2024 Burnaby Land Acknowledgement Guidelines wording. Include in all public-facing art plan documents.
burnaby.s2-ppap-requirements: Preliminary Public Art Plan required at rezoning. Must include site analysis, public art opportunities, proposed artwork types, preliminary budget, and timeline.
burnaby.s3-dpap-requirements: Detailed Public Art Plan submitted post-rezoning approval. Includes refined concept, artist shortlist or selection process, detailed budget, maintenance strategy.
burnaby.s3-civic-contribution: No separate civic contribution — program is developer-funded through rezoning conditions.
burnaby.s4-community-engagement: Community engagement required during art plan development. Methods determined in consultation with City staff.
burnaby.s4-indigenous-engagement: Engagement with local First Nations (Musqueam, Squamish, Tsleil-Waututh) encouraged. Must follow City reconciliation framework.
burnaby.s5-selection-process: Open call preferred. Invitational or direct commission permitted with City approval. Selection must follow approved art plan process.
burnaby.s5-selection-panel: Panel includes: City public art staff, community representatives, arts professionals, developer representative. City has final approval.
burnaby.s5-artist-eligibility: Project team members (architect, landscape architect, engineer) are barred from being the commissioned artist. Professional artists only.
burnaby.s7-contract-terms: Standard City artist agreement required. Includes copyright provisions, insurance, timeline, payment schedule, moral rights acknowledgement.
burnaby.s8-insurance: Artist must carry comprehensive general liability insurance. Amount specified in contract — typically $2M minimum.
burnaby.s8-materials-durability: Materials must be durable, low-maintenance, and appropriate for the public realm. Minimum 25-year lifespan expected. Anti-graffiti coating where appropriate.
burnaby.s10-siting: Artwork must be publicly accessible and visible from public realm. Siting plan approved by City. Integration with landscape and architecture required.
burnaby.s11-plaque: Interpretive plaque required as per City standards. Must include artist name, artwork title, date, medium, and land acknowledgement.
burnaby.s11-photography: Professional photography of completed artwork required. Minimum 6 high-resolution images from multiple angles, including context shots.
burnaby.s11-maintenance: Maintenance manual required from artist. Must include materials list, cleaning procedures, repair protocols, and recommended maintenance schedule.
burnaby.s11-documentation: Final documentation package: artist statement, artwork specifications, maintenance manual, budget reconciliation, professional photographs, plaque details.
burnaby.s11-registry: Artwork entered into City's public art inventory upon completion. Registry data includes location, artist, medium, dimensions, condition assessment.
burnaby.s11-ownership-transfer: Copyright remains with artist (moral rights). City receives unlimited license for documentation, promotion, and educational use. Physical artwork ownership transfers to City if on public land.
burnaby.s11-deaccessioning: City deaccessioning policy applies. Requires public consultation, artist notification, and Council approval for removal of public artworks.
burnaby.s11-maintenance-reserve: 10% of total public art budget must be allocated to maintenance reserve fund. Held by City for long-term artwork care.

north-vancouver-city.s1-eligibility: Voluntary program. Encouraged for: 10+ residential units OR 1,000+ sqm non-residential gross floor area. Applies to rezoning and development permit applications.
north-vancouver-city.s1-budget-calculation: 1% of construction costs encouraged (voluntary). Eligible costs include: art plan, artist selection, commission, design/materials/fabrication, site preparation, documentation, PR/unveiling event.
north-vancouver-city.s2-land-acknowledgement: Skwxwú7mesh (Squamish) and Səl̓ílwətaʔ/Selilwitulh (Tsleil-Waututh) peoples. Follow City of North Vancouver reconciliation protocols.
north-vancouver-city.s2-ppap-requirements: Public art consultant recommended. Preliminary plan outlines public art opportunities, potential locations, and proposed budget allocation.
north-vancouver-city.s3-dpap-requirements: Detailed plan includes artist selection process, artwork concept, detailed budget, timeline, and maintenance provisions.
north-vancouver-city.s4-community-engagement: Community engagement encouraged as part of art plan development. Scale appropriate to project size.
north-vancouver-city.s4-indigenous-engagement: Consultation with Squamish and Tsleil-Waututh Nations encouraged for projects on or near culturally significant sites.
north-vancouver-city.s5-selection-process: Open call, invitational, or direct commission. Public art consultant typically manages selection process.
north-vancouver-city.s5-selection-panel: Panel recommended to include: arts professionals, community members, developer representative, City staff advisor.
north-vancouver-city.s5-artist-eligibility: Professional artists preferred. No explicit bar on project team members but arm's-length process strongly recommended.
north-vancouver-city.s7-contract-terms: Artist agreement between developer and artist. City not a party to contract but reviews for compliance with art plan commitments.
north-vancouver-city.s8-insurance: Insurance requirements set by developer. City recommends minimum $2M CGL during fabrication and installation.
north-vancouver-city.s8-materials-durability: Materials appropriate for marine climate. Durable, low-maintenance. Weather-resistant finishes required for exterior works.
north-vancouver-city.s10-siting: Publicly visible and accessible location. Integration with building design and public realm. Must not impede pedestrian circulation.
north-vancouver-city.s11-plaque: Plaque as per CNV standard. An eligible cost within the public art budget. Includes artist, title, date, medium, brief description.
north-vancouver-city.s11-photography: Professional documentation photographs required for City records.
north-vancouver-city.s11-maintenance: Maintenance plan submitted with final documentation. Developer responsible for maintenance on private land.
north-vancouver-city.s11-documentation: Final package includes: artist bio/statement, artwork specifications, maintenance plan, as-built drawings, professional photographs.
north-vancouver-city.s11-registry: Artwork recorded in City's public art collection records.
north-vancouver-city.s11-ownership-transfer: Artwork on private land: developer retains ownership. Artwork on public land: ownership transfers to City. Copyright remains with artist.
north-vancouver-city.s11-deaccessioning: No formal deaccessioning policy for private-land artworks. City policy applies for public-land artworks.

north-vancouver-district.s1-eligibility: Rezoning applications. 5+ residential units OR 500+ sqm non-residential gross floor area. Bylaw 328545.
north-vancouver-district.s1-budget-calculation: 1% of gross construction costs on building permit. Voluntary program. Three options: A) Developer funds/City manages art selection, B) Developer funds and manages own selection, C) Contribute to Public Art Statutory Reserve Fund (projects <$25K or pooled contributions).
north-vancouver-district.s2-land-acknowledgement: Skwxwú7mesh (Squamish) and Səl̓ílwətaʔ/Selilwitulh (Tsleil-Waututh) peoples traditional territories.
north-vancouver-district.s2-ppap-requirements: Preliminary Public Art Plan submitted at rezoning. Includes site context, artwork opportunities, budget estimate, and proposed selection process.
north-vancouver-district.s3-dpap-requirements: Detailed Public Art Plan required before building permit. Must include finalized concept, artist selection results, detailed budget, maintenance plan, and timeline.
north-vancouver-district.s3-civic-contribution: Option C allows contribution to Public Art Statutory Reserve Fund for projects under $25K or where pooling is appropriate.
north-vancouver-district.s4-community-engagement: Community input opportunities required for publicly-sited artworks. Scale appropriate to project and location.
north-vancouver-district.s4-indigenous-engagement: Engagement with Squamish and Tsleil-Waututh Nations required for projects on culturally significant lands or involving Indigenous themes.
north-vancouver-district.s5-selection-process: Option A: City manages open call or invitational. Option B: Developer manages with District oversight. Selection process must be in approved art plan.
north-vancouver-district.s5-selection-panel: Panel includes: District residents, practicing artists, architect, landscape architect, developer representative. Minimum 5 members.
north-vancouver-district.s5-artist-eligibility: Professional artists. Project design team members may not serve as commissioned artist.
north-vancouver-district.s7-contract-terms: Option A: District contract with artist. Option B: Developer contract, reviewed by District. Standard terms include copyright, insurance, deliverables, payment schedule.
north-vancouver-district.s8-insurance: Artist carries CGL insurance during fabrication/installation. Minimum $2M. Developer carries post-installation insurance on private land.
north-vancouver-district.s8-materials-durability: Durable, weather-appropriate materials. Must withstand Pacific Northwest marine climate. Minimum 20-year expected lifespan.
north-vancouver-district.s10-siting: Publicly accessible and visible. On-site preferred. Must be integrated into landscape/architectural design. Siting approved by District.
north-vancouver-district.s11-plaque: Interpretive plaque required. Artist name, title, date, medium, brief artwork description.
north-vancouver-district.s11-photography: Minimum 6 professional high-resolution photographs from multiple angles and distances.
north-vancouver-district.s11-maintenance: Maintenance plan required from artist. District does NOT maintain artworks on private land. 10% of budget to maintenance reserve if artwork is on public land.
north-vancouver-district.s11-documentation: Final documentation: artist statement/bio, artwork specifications and materials, maintenance plan, final accounting/budget reconciliation, professional photographs.
north-vancouver-district.s11-registry: Artwork entered into District's public art registry. Includes location, artist, medium, dimensions, condition, maintenance schedule.
north-vancouver-district.s11-ownership-transfer: Private land: developer retains ownership, must maintain. Public land: ownership transfers to District. Copyright remains with artist per Canadian Copyright Act.
north-vancouver-district.s11-deaccessioning: District deaccessioning procedures apply for public-land artworks. Requires assessment, artist consultation, community notification, and Council resolution.
north-vancouver-district.s11-maintenance-reserve: 10% of public art budget allocated to maintenance reserve for artworks on public land. Not applicable for private-land artworks.

new-westminster.s1-eligibility: Capital projects over $1M: 1% contribution. Projects $500K–$1M: 0.5% contribution. Applies to both civic and private sector projects.
new-westminster.s1-budget-calculation: Civic: 1% of capital project costs (>$1M) or 0.5% ($500K–$1M). Also receives $2/citizen annual contribution from property taxes for Public Art Fund.
new-westminster.s2-land-acknowledgement: Halkomelem-speaking peoples. Decolonial practices integrated into public art program. Reconciliation is a stated program priority.
new-westminster.s2-ppap-requirements: Preliminary Public Art Plan as part of development application. Identifies opportunities, proposed approach, budget, and timeline.
new-westminster.s3-dpap-requirements: Detailed plan with refined concept, artist selection process, community engagement strategy, budget breakdown, and maintenance provisions.
new-westminster.s3-civic-contribution: $2 per citizen annual contribution from property taxes funds civic Public Art Fund. Supplements developer contributions.
new-westminster.s4-community-engagement: Meaningful community engagement required. Arts and Culture Advisory Committee (AAC) reviews all public art proposals.
new-westminster.s4-indigenous-engagement: Reconciliation priority. Engagement with local First Nations using decolonial frameworks. Indigenous art practices and perspectives centered.
new-westminster.s5-selection-process: Three methods: Open call, invitational (limited competition), or direct award. Method selected based on project scope, budget, and context.
new-westminster.s5-selection-panel: Arts and Culture Advisory Committee (AAC): 15 members including Council representatives, arts council members, practicing artists, urban designers, and community representatives.
new-westminster.s5-artist-eligibility: Professional artists. Emerging artists encouraged for smaller commissions. No explicit project-team bar but conflict-of-interest policy applies.
new-westminster.s7-contract-terms: City standard artist agreement. Includes moral rights provisions, copyright license, insurance, payment milestones, and warranty period.
new-westminster.s8-insurance: Comprehensive general liability required. Amount per City risk management assessment, typically $2M–$5M depending on project scale.
new-westminster.s8-materials-durability: Durable materials suitable for public realm. Materials review by City engineering/parks staff. Climate-appropriate for Fraser Valley conditions.
new-westminster.s10-siting: Publicly accessible location. Priority to high-traffic areas, civic facilities, parks, and waterfront. Integrated with urban design objectives.
new-westminster.s11-plaque: Interpretive plaque per City standards. Includes artist name, title, date, medium, land acknowledgement, and brief artwork description.
new-westminster.s11-photography: Professional photographs required. Digital high-resolution images for City archives and promotion.
new-westminster.s11-maintenance: Maintenance plan from artist required. City assumes maintenance responsibility for civic collection artworks.
new-westminster.s11-documentation: Complete documentation package: artist statement, specifications, maintenance plan, budget reconciliation, photographs, plaque text.
new-westminster.s11-registry: All artworks entered into City's public art registry/inventory. Publicly accessible database maintained by Cultural Services.
new-westminster.s11-ownership-transfer: Civic artworks: City owns physical work. Copyright stays with artist. City receives broad license for reproduction, promotion, educational purposes.
new-westminster.s11-deaccessioning: Formal deaccessioning process defined in policy. Requires AAC review, public consultation, artist notification, and Council approval. Criteria include: condition, relevance, safety, cost of maintenance.

port-moody.s1-eligibility: Developer contribution is VOLUNTARY. Encouraged for all significant development applications. 0.6% of construction budget as guideline.
port-moody.s1-budget-calculation: Voluntary 0.6% of construction budget. Tiered allocation: ≤$400K → integrate artwork into development; $400K–$2.5M → 60% on-site artwork + 40% to reserves; >$2.5M → 60% on-site artwork + 40% split across trust/facility reserves.
port-moody.s2-land-acknowledgement: kwikwəƛ̓əm (Kwikwetlem) First Nation and Coast Salish peoples. Land acknowledgement in program materials and public art signage.
port-moody.s2-ppap-requirements: Preliminary plan at development application stage. Outlines art integration opportunities, preliminary budget, and proposed artist engagement approach.
port-moody.s3-dpap-requirements: Detailed plan with finalized concept, selected artist, budget breakdown, community engagement results, maintenance strategy, and installation timeline.
port-moody.s3-civic-contribution: Four reserve funds receive voluntary developer contributions: Arts Reserve (50%), Public Art Reserve (20%), Public Art Maintenance Reserve (10%), Arts Facility Reserve (20%).
port-moody.s4-community-engagement: Community participation required in art selection and development. Public engagement events and feedback mechanisms expected.
port-moody.s4-indigenous-engagement: Consultation with Indigenous Relations Manager for any works involving First Nations themes, materials, or cultural content. Deaccessioning of First Nations works requires this consultation.
port-moody.s5-selection-process: Open calls preferred. Geographically limited calls permitted (BC artists, regional focus). Community participation in selection process required.
port-moody.s5-selection-panel: Panel includes arts professionals, community members, City staff, and developer representative. Indigenous representation for relevant projects.
port-moody.s5-artist-eligibility: Professional and emerging artists. BC-based artists may be given preference in geographically limited calls.
port-moody.s7-contract-terms: City standard contract for civic projects. Developer contracts reviewed by City for compliance. Includes moral rights, copyright, insurance, warranty.
port-moody.s8-insurance: CGL insurance required during fabrication and installation. Amount per City requirements.
port-moody.s8-materials-durability: Durable, low-maintenance materials appropriate for Pacific Northwest coastal climate. Weather-resistant finishes. Anti-graffiti treatment where warranted.
port-moody.s10-siting: Publicly accessible and visible. Priority to civic facilities, parks, trails, and waterfront areas. Must integrate with site design.
port-moody.s11-plaque: Interpretive signage required. Includes artist name, title, date, medium, and brief description of artwork concept.
port-moody.s11-photography: 6 high-resolution professional photographs required. Multiple angles, detail shots, and context views.
port-moody.s11-maintenance: Maintenance plan required from artist. 10% of overall public art budget allocated to maintenance. City maintains civic collection.
port-moody.s11-documentation: Final package: artist bio, artist statement, 6+ high-resolution photos, maintenance plan, budget reconciliation, as-built specifications.
port-moody.s11-registry: Artwork entered into City's public art collection database.
port-moody.s11-ownership-transfer: Civic artworks: City ownership. Private-land artworks: developer ownership with maintenance responsibility. Copyright stays with artist.
port-moody.s11-deaccessioning: Deaccessioning process requires: condition assessment, public consultation, artist notification, and Council approval. Consultation with Indigenous Relations Manager required for First Nations works.
port-moody.s11-maintenance-reserve: 10% of public art budget allocated to Public Art Maintenance Reserve. Separate from Arts Reserve and Arts Facility Reserve.

surrey.s1-eligibility: 10+ multi-family residential units OR 1,000+ sqm non-residential gross floor area. Applies to development applications.
surrey.s1-budget-calculation: Civic: 1.25% of construction costs for applicable capital projects. Private: 0.50% of total construction cost (excludes land, offsite servicing) as of Jan 2018, reviewed biannually. Contributions >$200K: option to install on-site artwork or pay cash-in-lieu.
surrey.s2-land-acknowledgement: Semiahmoo, Katzie, Kwantlen, and other Coast Salish peoples. Land acknowledgement per City of Surrey protocols.
surrey.s2-ppap-requirements: Preliminary Public Art Plan at development application. Three-step process: Preliminary Plan → Detailed Plan → Final Report.
surrey.s3-dpap-requirements: Detailed Public Art Plan with refined concept, artist selection, community engagement plan, detailed budget, timeline, and maintenance strategy.
surrey.s3-civic-contribution: Civic program funded at 1.25% of capital project construction costs. Separate from private developer contributions.
surrey.s4-community-engagement: Community engagement per approved Public Art Plan. Scale appropriate to project size and public visibility.
surrey.s4-indigenous-engagement: Engagement with local First Nations for projects on traditional territories or involving Indigenous themes and cultural expression.
surrey.s5-selection-process: Open call standard. Invitational permitted for projects with specific artistic vision. Direct commission for special circumstances with City approval.
surrey.s5-selection-panel: Selection panel includes: arts professionals, community representatives, City public art staff, project stakeholders.
surrey.s5-artist-eligibility: Project team members (architect, landscape architect, engineer) cannot be the commissioned artist. Professional artists required.
surrey.s7-contract-terms: City standard artist agreement. Copyright provisions, insurance requirements, payment schedule, warranty terms, moral rights acknowledgement.
surrey.s8-insurance: Comprehensive general liability insurance required. Minimum per City standards.
surrey.s8-materials-durability: Materials must be durable, low-maintenance, and weather-appropriate. Projected artwork lifespan of approximately 50 years. Anti-graffiti coating required for accessible surfaces.
surrey.s10-siting: Publicly accessible and visible from public realm. Integration with site and building design. Must enhance public space quality.
surrey.s11-plaque: Interpretive plaque per City standards. Artist name, title, date, medium, and artwork description.
surrey.s11-photography: Professional photographs for City records and public art registry.
surrey.s11-maintenance: 10% of public art allocation for long-term maintenance. Maintenance plan required from artist.
surrey.s11-documentation: Final report: artist statement, specifications, maintenance plan, budget reconciliation, professional photographs, plaque details.
surrey.s11-registry: All public artworks entered into City's public art registry/collection database.
surrey.s11-ownership-transfer: Artwork on public land transfers to City ownership. Copyright remains with artist. City receives license for documentation and promotion.
surrey.s11-deaccessioning: City deaccessioning procedures apply. Assessment criteria, public process, artist notification, Council approval required.
surrey.s11-maintenance-reserve: 10% of public art allocation dedicated to long-term maintenance fund.

coquitlam.s1-eligibility: Developer contributions are VOLUNTARY. No mandatory thresholds — program relies on conversations between developers and City staff during development review.
coquitlam.s1-budget-calculation: No mandatory percentage. Three streams: Community (grants/partnerships), Civic (capital project allocations), Developer-Initiated (voluntary contributions). Budget negotiated case-by-case.
coquitlam.s2-land-acknowledgement: kwikwəƛ̓əm (Kwikwetlem), Sḵwx̱wú7mesh (Squamish), stó:lō and Coast Salish peoples. City reconciliation protocols apply.
coquitlam.s2-ppap-requirements: No standardized preliminary plan template. Developers discuss public art opportunities with City Planning and Culture staff during application review.
coquitlam.s3-dpap-requirements: Detailed plan developed collaboratively between developer, artist, and City interdepartmental team.
coquitlam.s3-civic-contribution: Civic program contributions included in capital project operating funds. No fixed percentage — determined by interdepartmental team review.
coquitlam.s4-community-engagement: Community engagement encouraged. Interdepartmental team includes community perspectives through Parks, Recreation & Culture department.
coquitlam.s4-indigenous-engagement: Engagement with local First Nations for culturally significant projects. Follows City reconciliation framework.
coquitlam.s5-selection-process: Varies by stream. Developer-initiated: developer manages with City oversight. Civic: City manages through interdepartmental team. Open calls and invitational both used.
coquitlam.s5-selection-panel: Interdepartmental team: Planning, Strategic Initiatives, Engineering, Parks/Recreation/Culture, Corporate Services. External arts advisors for civic projects.
coquitlam.s5-artist-eligibility: Professional artists preferred. No explicit project-team bar but arm's-length process recommended.
coquitlam.s7-contract-terms: Contract terms vary by stream. Civic projects use City standard agreement. Developer projects: City reviews for compliance with program objectives.
coquitlam.s8-insurance: Insurance requirements per City standards. Set in artist agreement.
coquitlam.s8-materials-durability: Durable, low-maintenance materials. Climate-appropriate for Coquitlam conditions. Materials review by Engineering department.
coquitlam.s10-siting: Publicly accessible preferred. Integration with development and public realm design. Siting reviewed by interdepartmental team.
coquitlam.s11-plaque: Interpretive signage expected for publicly-sited works.
coquitlam.s11-photography: Professional documentation photographs for City records.
coquitlam.s11-maintenance: Maintenance included in operating funds tied to capital projects. Developer responsible for private-land artworks.
coquitlam.s11-documentation: Documentation requirements vary by project scale. Standard package includes artist info, specifications, maintenance notes, photographs.
coquitlam.s11-registry: Artwork tracked in City cultural asset records.
coquitlam.s11-ownership-transfer: Civic artworks: City ownership. Developer artworks: developer ownership. Copyright per Canadian Copyright Act.
coquitlam.s11-deaccessioning: No formal deaccessioning policy documented. Handled case-by-case through interdepartmental review.

squamish.s1-eligibility: Civic: Capital projects over $1M. Developer: Voluntary through Community Amenity Contributions (CACs). No mandatory development thresholds.
squamish.s1-budget-calculation: Civic: 1% of capital project costs (>$1M). Developer: Voluntary CAC — can install art on-site or contribute to Public Art Fund. Max 10% of fund used for program administration.
squamish.s2-land-acknowledgement: Sḵwx̱wú7mesh Úxwumixw (Squamish Nation) traditional territory. Protocol agreements with Squamish Nation apply.
squamish.s2-ppap-requirements: Public Art Plan for civic projects developed by Public Art Advisor (external not-for-profit). Developer projects: plan developed in consultation with City.
squamish.s3-dpap-requirements: Detailed plan includes concept, artist, budget, timeline, community engagement approach, and maintenance provisions.
squamish.s3-civic-contribution: 1% of capital project costs over $1M. Public Art Fund also receives voluntary developer CACs.
squamish.s4-community-engagement: Community engagement as determined by Public Art Advisor and City staff. Scale appropriate to project.
squamish.s4-indigenous-engagement: Meaningful engagement with Squamish Nation for all significant public art projects. Nation-to-Nation relationship framework.
squamish.s5-selection-process: Public Art Advisor (external not-for-profit) manages selection for civic projects. Developer projects: various approaches with City input.
squamish.s5-selection-panel: Panel assembled by Public Art Advisor. Includes community members, arts professionals, and City staff.
squamish.s5-artist-eligibility: Professional artists. Mass-produced items, business logos, directional signage, and historical artifacts are ineligible as public art.
squamish.s7-contract-terms: Standard agreement for civic commissions. Developer contracts reviewed for alignment with Public Art Policy.
squamish.s8-insurance: Insurance per City/Public Art Advisor requirements.
squamish.s8-materials-durability: Durable, weather-appropriate materials for Squamish climate (rain, wind, temperature variation). Low-maintenance construction.
squamish.s10-siting: Publicly accessible locations. Priority to civic buildings, parks, waterfront, and high-traffic public spaces.
squamish.s11-plaque: Interpretive plaque with artist info, title, date, medium, and artwork description.
squamish.s11-photography: Professional photography for program records and promotion.
squamish.s11-maintenance: Maintenance plan required. $5K–$20K of Public Art Provision Fund set aside for special maintenance needs.
squamish.s11-documentation: Final documentation package per Public Art Advisor requirements.
squamish.s11-registry: Artwork entered into District/Public Art Advisor's public art inventory.
squamish.s11-ownership-transfer: Civic artworks: District of Squamish ownership. Copyright retained by artist.
squamish.s11-deaccessioning: Deaccessioning procedures through Public Art Advisor with City approval. Public consultation and artist notification.
squamish.s11-maintenance-reserve: $5K–$20K from Public Art Provision Fund allocated for special maintenance. Separate from regular operations budget.

white-rock.s1-eligibility: Civic: Large capital projects (1.25% contribution). Developer: No mandatory formula — staff encourages public art contribution at application stage.
white-rock.s1-budget-calculation: Civic: 1.25% of large capital project costs. Developer: No mandatory formula. $50K annual contribution to Community Amenity Contribution Reserve. PAAC advises on 3–5 year rolling workplan.
white-rock.s2-land-acknowledgement: Semiahmoo First Nation traditional territory. City reconciliation commitments apply.
white-rock.s2-ppap-requirements: Public art proposals reviewed by PAAC (Public Art Advisory Committee). Developers encouraged to engage PAAC early in design process.
white-rock.s3-dpap-requirements: Detailed plan reviewed by PAAC. Includes concept, artist selection approach, budget, timeline, and maintenance.
white-rock.s3-civic-contribution: 1.25% of large capital projects. $50K annual from Community Amenity Contribution Reserve supplements program.
white-rock.s4-community-engagement: PAAC provides community perspective. Public engagement for significant civic art projects.
white-rock.s4-indigenous-engagement: Engagement with Semiahmoo First Nation for projects on traditional territory or involving Indigenous cultural content.
white-rock.s5-selection-process: PAAC reviews and recommends. Open calls, invitational, and direct commission all used depending on project scope.
white-rock.s5-selection-panel: PAAC: advisory committee to Council. Reviews proposals, recommends artists, advises on program priorities.
white-rock.s5-artist-eligibility: Local artist preference: White Rock, South Surrey, or Semiahmoo First Nations artists given priority consideration.
white-rock.s7-contract-terms: City standard terms for civic commissions. Private sector encouraged to use PAAC-reviewed agreements.
white-rock.s8-insurance: Insurance per City risk management requirements.
white-rock.s8-materials-durability: Durable, weather-resistant materials suitable for marine/coastal environment. Low-maintenance construction preferred.
white-rock.s10-siting: Publicly accessible locations. Waterfront, civic facilities, and town centre priority. Integration with placemaking objectives.
white-rock.s11-plaque: Interpretive plaque per City standards. Artist, title, date, medium, description.
white-rock.s11-photography: Professional photographs for City records and public art inventory.
white-rock.s11-maintenance: Maintenance plan required. City maintains civic collection artworks.
white-rock.s11-documentation: Final documentation including artist info, specifications, maintenance plan, photographs.
white-rock.s11-registry: Artwork entered into City's public art inventory.
white-rock.s11-ownership-transfer: Civic artworks: City ownership. Copyright retained by artist. City receives documentation and promotion license.
white-rock.s11-deaccessioning: PAAC advises on deaccessioning. Council approval required. Public consultation and artist notification.
